Memory summary

The solution in solution.py implements the routed and always-active shared experts in hand-written CUDA C++ with inline SM90 PTX, compiled through load_inline. The official correctness check passed, and the final audit judged the run clean. The benchmark failed at its third shape, T=1, due to a dynamic shared-memory attribute setup bug. The official peak_fraction is null, so the run has no publishable score.

Relevant prior context

The agent confirmed an NVIDIA H100 PCIe (SM90), CUDA 12.8, and PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128. The initial extension build failed because the system CUDA include tree had a broken cusparse.h symlink; adding include paths from installed NVIDIA packages fixed the build. PTX primitive checks passed for the SM90 instructions used.

The solution builds a device-side expert grouping pipeline: count routed and shared slots, scan counts into padded expert tiles, and scatter token IDs and routing weights. Shared experts enter the same grouped path as routed experts, with weight 1.0. The first grouped GEMM computes gate and up projections together with BF16 MMA and writes silu(gate) * up to a BF16 intermediate. The second grouped GEMM applies the down projection, scales routed outputs by their live expert weights, and accumulates them into an FP32 output with vector atomic adds. A final kernel converts the result to BF16.

During development, a concurrent checker and benchmark caused an OOM and contended measurements. The agent later ran sequential checks; the audit’s final isolated regrade also passed correctness.

Important non-obvious context

The benchmark processes shapes in order: T = 4096, 4127, 1, 8192, 512, 1000. Its first two shapes select BM=128; T=1 selects BM=16. The checker caps token counts at 256, so all correctness cases selected BM=16 and did not exercise this specialization transition after BM=128.

The source’s set_smem_once uses a function-local static byte count templated on the kernel function-pointer type. That cache is shared across specializations of a given kernel, so after BM=128 sets the attribute, the later BM=16 specialization skips its own cudaFuncSetAttribute call. Its launch requests dynamic shared memory that was never enabled for that specialization, producing CUDA error: invalid argument. Running T=1 alone in a fresh process succeeded because BM=16 was then the first specialization. A robust fix is to set the attribute for every kernel specialization, or track setup per specialization rather than in a shared static.

The official H100 compute reference peak was 756 BF16 TFLOPS. The first two shapes produced partial measurements, but the benchmark did not finish, so their fractions do not constitute an official aggregate score.
